fullPassage: On-screen, climate disaster is everywhere you look, but the scope of the world's climate transformation may just as quickly eliminate the climate-fiction genre — indeed eliminate any effort to tell the story of warming, which could grow too large and too obvious even for Hollywood. You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a marginal feature of human life. But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, hardly anyone will be able to feel isolated from its impacts. And so as climate change expands across the horizon, it may cease to be a story. Why watch or read climate fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window? At the moment, stories illustrating global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. But when we can no longer pretend that climate suffering is distant — in time or in place — we will stop pretending about it and start pretending within it.

④ reduce(줄이다): 완전히 없애는 것과 다르고 반대말도 아님

questions.passage:
(A) When the temperature rises by three or four more <u>degrees</u>, life on the planet will change.
(B) She earned two <u>degrees</u> in science before working at the research center.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)의 밑줄 친 degrees의 문맥적 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) degrees = (온도의) 도, (B) degrees = 학위
det.analysis:
(A) 'the temperature rises by three or four more degrees'는 기온이 몇 '도(degrees)' 오른다는 뜻이에요 → (온도의) 도

(B) 'earned two degrees in science'는 과학 분야에서 두 개의 '학위(degrees)'를 땄다는 뜻이에요 → 학위

따라서 (A) (온도의) 도 - (B) 학위인 ②가 정답 ← 정답

같은 degrees라도 문맥에 따라 '온도의 도'와 '학위'로 다르게 해석돼요

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a particular style or category of literature, art, or film"

det.korean: 영영풀이 정답: genre(장르)
det.analysis:
정의: '문학·예술·영화의 특정한 양식이나 범주' = genre(장르)

① feature: '특징' — 정의와 다름

② genre: '장르' — 정의에 부합 ← 정답

③ effort: '노력' — 정의와 다름

④ horizon: '지평선' — 정의와 다름

questions.passage: But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, hardly anyone will be able to feel __________ (isolate) from its impacts.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (1단어) (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: isolate → isolated: 'feel + 과거분사'로 '고립된 (느낌을 받다)'라는 수동·상태의 의미
det.analysis: 빈칸은 'feel __________ from its impacts'에서 감정·상태를 나타내는 자리예요. 'feel + 과거분사(p.p.)'는 '~한 상태로 느끼다'라는 뜻이므로 동사 isolate를 과거분사 isolated로 바꿔요. '(영향에서) 고립된 느낌을 받다'라는 의미가 돼요.

questions.passage: At the moment, stories __________ (illustrate) global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (1단어) (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: illustrate → illustrating: 명사 stories를 뒤에서 꾸미는 현재분사(능동)
det.analysis: 빈칸은 명사 stories 뒤에서 그 명사를 꾸며 주는 자리예요. '이야기가 지구온난화를 보여 주는' 능동의 관계이므로 현재분사 illustrating으로 바꿔요. 'stories illustrating global warming'은 '지구온난화를 보여 주는 이야기'라는 뜻이에요.

questions.passage: On-screen, climate disaster is everywhere you look, but the scope of the world's climate transformation may just as quickly eliminate the climate-fiction genre — indeed eliminate any effort to tell the story of warming, which could grow too large and too obvious even for Hollywood. You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a marginal feature of human life. But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, hardly anyone will be able to feel isolated from its impacts. And so as climate change expands across the horizon, it may __________. Why watch or read climate fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window? At the moment, stories illustrating global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. But when we can no longer pretend that climate suffering is distant — in time or in place — we will stop pretending about it and start pretending within it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸: cease to be a story(이야기이기를 멈추다) — 기후 변화가 보편화되면 이야기로 성립하지 못함
det.analysis:
앞에서 기후 변화의 규모가 너무 커져 이야기하려는 노력조차 사라질 수 있다고 했어요. 그러니 기후 변화가 지평선 너머로 확장되면 그것은 더 이상 '이야기이기를 멈출(cease to be a story)' 수 있다는 흐름이에요.

① cease to be a story (이야기이기를 멈추다): 규모가 커져 이야기로 성립 못 한다는 흐름에 맞아 정답 ← 정답

② become a global hit (세계적 흥행작이 되다): 흐름과 반대

③ attract more viewers (더 많은 관객을 끌다): 흐름과 반대

④ change its main genre (주요 장르를 바꾸다): 본문에 없는 내용
det.tip: cease to be a story = 더 이상 이야기가 아니게 되다

questions.passage: On-screen, climate disaster is everywhere you look, but the scope of the world's climate transformation may just as quickly eliminate the climate-fiction genre — indeed eliminate any effort to tell the story of warming, which could grow too large and too obvious even for Hollywood. You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a marginal feature of human life. But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, hardly anyone will be able to feel isolated from its impacts. And so as climate change expands across the horizon, it may cease to be a story. Why watch or read climate fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window? At the moment, stories illustrating global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. But when we can no longer pretend that climate suffering is distant — in time or in place — we will stop pretending about it and __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸: start pretending within it(그 안에서 (~인) 척하기 시작하다) — '그것에 관해(about)'에서 '그 안에서(within)'로의 전환
det.analysis:
빈칸 앞은 '기후 고통이 멀다고 더 이상 가정할 수 없게 되면, 우리는 그것에 관해(about) 가정하기를 멈출 것'이라는 흐름이에요. 그 대조로, 이제는 그 현실 '안에서(within)' 살아가며 (~인) 척하기 시작한다는 내용이 와야 대구가 완성돼요.

① return to our normal life (평범한 일상으로 돌아가다): 대조 구조와 맞지 않음

② forget the whole crisis (위기 전체를 잊다): 흐름과 반대

③ escape from reality forever (영원히 현실에서 도피하다): 현실을 직면한다는 흐름과 반대

④ start pretending within it (그 안에서 (~인) 척하기 시작하다): about → within의 대조에 맞아 정답 ← 정답
det.tip: stop pretending about it ↔ start pretending within it (관해 → 안에서)
